claims.text: A thin, conformal h-BN coating on CoCrFeNi will reduce coefficient of friction at every tested temperature from 25 °C to 800 °C relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi.
A thin, conformal h-BN coating on CoCrFeNi will reduce wear rate at every tested temperature from 25 °C to 800 °C relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi.
h-BN has a layered structure with weak interlayer forces that provides low shear strength and lubricity at ambient temperature.
h-BN possesses sufficient thermal stability to remain an effective lubricating layer up to 800 °C under sliding.
h-BN is sufficiently oxidation-resistant in ambient or slightly oxidizing environments throughout the 25–800 °C test range.
The coating will retain its integrity during sliding at elevated temperatures.
Retention of the h-BN layer will prevent or suppress formation of abrasive oxides.
Retention of the h-BN layer will mitigate adhesive wear.
The h-BN interface will self-adapt to shifts in the dominant wear mechanisms as temperature changes.
Uncoated CoCrFeNi has temperature-dependent tribological performance.
The friction coefficient of uncoated CoCrFeNi increases or otherwise changes as temperature rises.
The wear rate of uncoated CoCrFeNi increases or otherwise changes with temperature.
Temperature-induced structural and defect changes in a high-entropy alloy can alter its friction response.
The proposed intervention is limited to sliding contact between approximately 25 °C and 800 °C under ambient or slightly oxidizing conditions.
The magnitude of friction and wear improvement may depend on coating uniformity, coating thickness, and sliding-test parameters.
